newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude slips on weakness in U.S. gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude slips on weakness in U.S. gasoline.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures slipped back on Friday afternoon from the day's highs in response to weakness in U.S. gasoline markets, traders said.
Dec Brent was just 10 cents a barrel firmer at 1431 GMT, trading at $23.85, after earlier reaching a high of $24.05.
Nov gas oil was unchanged at $223.75 a tonne.
"It has just come off with gasoline in the U.S.," one London dealer said. "There are no fresh stories that I can see."
MeesPierson Derivatives said in a daily report that support for Brent lay at $23.65, with resistance at the day's high of $24.05.
The market had rallied on Thursday amid rumours of problems with major Texas refineries, even though regulators there said they were not aware of any major problems.
"It may be that the problems are not as serious as we had thought," a trader said.

Gasoline prices in the U.S. have been influential in world energy markets in the past few days, with latest data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) showing that stocks are over eight million barrels down on year-ago levels.
Gasoline remained a key market to watch.
"With the rumours of refinery problems yesterday, anything fresh on that would be of interest," a trader said.
Nov NYMEX gasoline was 57 cents down at 68.65 cents a gallon.
